title: A suggestion becomes focus only when accepted
lead: The proposed local assistant distinguishes a predicted-target halo from actual keyboard focus. In enabled contexts, Tab accepts the visible suggestion and moves focus; it does not activate the target or complete an autonomous task.

title: Helpful assistance preserves a way through the page
lead: Uncertainty and stale targets return control to ordinary navigation. Escape, reverse navigation, and application editing shortcuts retain their meaning. Site and context compatibility are part of the product's usefulness.

title: Separate human feedback from the system's own echo
lead: Showing a suggestion, moving focus, and seeing meaningful subsequent interaction are different events. Treating extension-produced focus as confirmation would manufacture a self-reinforcing training signal.

title: Evaluate each new personal checkpoint
lead: Acceptance alone can be ambiguous. Controlled feedback, retained provenance, separate recording and training controls, and rollback let personalization follow the person without requiring continuous background weight updates.

title: Prove one useful workflow before broadening the scope
lead: Start on a limited site with a small ranking baseline. Shadow predictions reveal errors before anything moves; visible suggestions and opt-in acceptance follow only when evidence supports them.

title: The destination is useful work completed with less waiting
lead: The checked autonomous runner and explicit hybrid mode extend the same foundation. The final gate is faster completed tasks at a predeclared reliability level, while predictive Tab remains a small user-controlled moment built on that evidence.
